{{eastern name order|Medgyessy Pál}}
'''Pál Medgyessy''' (October 19, 1919, in [[Egercsehi]] – October 8, 1977, in [[Budapest]]) was a mathematician, [[Doctor of Sciences|Doctor of Mathematical Sciences]] (1973).

==Biography==
He graduated at the [[Eötvös Loránd University|University of Budapest]] as a student of Eötvös József Collegium<!--Q966634-->. He started his career as a trainee at the Institute of Medical Physics at the [[University of Debrecen]]. Due to his illness, his scientific work was slow to develop.

He read the [[Latin]]-language classics in the original, spoke [[German language|German]], [[French language|French]], and [[Italian language|Italian]] well, and during his captivity he also mastered [[Russian language|Russian]], so his skills were utilised as an interpreter during the war. He published some of his books in English.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20160304094949/http://www.szabarchiv.hu/drupal/userfiles/file/Medgyessy%20P%C3%A1l%20a%20sokoldal%C3%BA%20tud%C3%B3s%20matematikus.pdf Medgyessy Pál, a sokoldalú tudós matematikus] ("Pál Medgyessy, the multi-faceted scholar mathematician", an article by Zoltán Rostás)</ref>

He was an aspirant to the candidate's degree at the Mathematical Research Institute of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]], a student of [[Alfréd Rényi]]’s. From 1955 on he was a research associate and scientific advisor at the Institute. He received his doctorate in mathematics from the HAS in 1973.

==Research interests==
His main research interests were [[probability]], [[mathematical statistics]], and their applications; his results on numerical methods are also remarkable. Many of his papers are in the fields of [[medicine]], [[biology]], [[chemistry]], and [[spectroscopy]]. His results on various [[Mechanical calculator|non-electronic calculators and equipment]] are noteworthy.

He was an outstanding expert in [[bibliography]], credited with the modernization of the mathematics section of the [[Dewey Decimal Classification|decimal classification]] and the preparation of several bibliographies, including those of the works of [[Frigyes Riesz]] and [[Alfréd Rényi]].
 
His works on the history of science deal with ancient [[Babylonia]]n and [[Ancient Egypt|Egyptian]] science and the history of [[Chinese mathematics]] and [[Chinese astrology|astrology]].

==Major works==
===In English===
* ''Decompositions of Superposition of Distribution Functions'' (Bp., 1961), its 1995 edition: {{ISBN|978-1-4899-5624-8}}
* ''Decomposition of Superpositions of Density Functions and Discrete Distributions'' ([[New York City|New York]], 1977). {{ISBN|978-0852742945}}.

===In Hungarian===
* ''Valószínűségeloszlás-függvények keverékének felbontása összetevőire'' ("Decomposition of mixtures of probability distribution functions into its components", Budapest, 1954)
* ''Valószínűségszámítás'' ("Probability theory", textbook, authored with Lajos Takács, Budapest, 1957, 1966)
* ''Sűrűségfüggvények és diszkrét eloszlások szuperpozíciójának felbontása'' ("Decomposition of density functions and superposition of discrete distributions", Budapest, 1971)
* ''Rényi Alfréd munkássága'' ("The Works of Alfréd Rényi", compiled, Budapest, 1971)
